sections.subtopic: ⭐ Mock Trial — three consecutive state championships
sections.preview: The strongest competitive achievement Trinity has, and it is academic rather than athletic. It appears in neither School Profile PDF and was found only by enumerating the blog. - Competition: the North Carolina Bar Foundation's annual Mock Trial competition - Level: Middle School - Team size: 15 students - Coach:…
sections.text:
**The strongest competitive achievement Trinity has, and it is academic rather than
athletic.** It appears in **neither** School Profile PDF and was found only by
enumerating the blog.

- Competition: the **North Carolina Bar Foundation**'s annual Mock Trial competition
- Level: **Middle School**
- Team size: **15 students**
- Coach: **Jennifer Bader**
- **Champions in 2023, 2024 and 2025 — three consecutive years**

The second-year championship was competed at the **Mecklenburg County Courthouse on
Dec. 8**, against **five other middle school teams**. Individual student recognitions
were published; per the rule above they are counted, not named.

Coach **Jennifer Bader**, verbatim:
> "I think one thing that sets our team apart is how well our attorneys can argue the
> rules of evidence and handle objections."

> "I just love when the light bulb comes on for kids. It's really challenging material,
> but they really get into it."

sections.subtopic: Speech & Debate — also a state champion, and also a class
sections.preview: From "Celebrating TES Staculty Achievements", verbatim: > "The speech and debate and mock trial teams both won their respective state > championships this year." Speech & Debate is simultaneously a 7th-grade weekly enrichment (per the profile PDF's enrichment list) and a competitive team — i.e. it is both a class and…
sections.text:
From "Celebrating TES Staculty Achievements", verbatim:

> "The **speech and debate and mock trial teams both won their respective state
> championships this year.**"

**Speech & Debate is simultaneously a 7th-grade weekly enrichment** (per the profile
PDF's enrichment list) **and a competitive team** — i.e. it is both a class and a club.
Worth stating explicitly, because listing it only as an enrichment understates it.

**Jennifer Bader** is **Speech and Debate and Mock Trial Team Coach**, and has served as
**Forensics Committee Chair** and a board member of the **North Carolina Association for
Scholastic Activities**.

sections.text:
From `/spirituality/honor-code.cfm`, verbatim:

> "A group of honor council members who are **elected by their grade level peers in
> Middle School** are responsible for encouraging integrity, for creating a community of
> trust that is core to our academic community and in life, and for holding fellow
> students to the expectations set out in the pledge."

**The Honor Code was created by students in 2002.** The Middle School **Honor Pledge**
was adopted in **2012**, verbatim:

> "As a child of God, I pledge that I have not cheated by giving or receiving help on
> this work, including plagiarizing. Moreover, I am unaware of any violation of this
> pledge by other students."

The Honor Code itself carries six pledges: responsibility, doing one's best, respecting
others' uniqueness, kindness, celebrating joy and beauty, and refraining from dishonesty
or theft.

General leadership framing from `/admission/k-8-advantage.cfm`, verbatim:
> "eighth graders often find themselves as the captains of sports teams, **leading honor
> councils**, and assuming the leading roles in school productions."

sections.text:
Verbatim from the 2026-27 School Profile:

> "**Student Clubs & Groups: Lower School-** Chess Club, Girls on the Run & Let Me Run,
> Young Children of Color, **Middle School-** Odyssey of the Mind, Young People of Color,
> Young People for Social Justice Group, Gender Sexuality Alliance Group, Radagast
> Rabies, Creative Writing, Climate Justice, Koinonia Representatives, Honor Council,
> Invisible Differences, Spirituality and Chapel Music, Monday Math Mania"

**Only 6 of the 15 are corroborated anywhere on the website.** Zero web hits for:
Odyssey of the Mind, Radagast Rabies, Climate Justice, Monday Math Mania, Let Me Run,
Spirituality and Chapel Music, Creative Writing (which appears only as a teacher's
conference topic, not a club).

**Two are corroborated but in a different character than "club":**
- **Chess Club** — corroborated only as a **paid TED after-school enrichment**
 ("for an additional fee"), not as a student club.
- **Girls on the Run** — corroborated: Trinity was the organization's **second
 independent-school chapter**, it "continues to be a popular program for students in
 **grades 3-5**", and founder **Molly Barker** is a Trinity alumni parent.

**Invisible Differences is a PARENT group, not a student club** — see the affinity-groups
file. The profile PDF lists it under student clubs, which conflicts with the school's own
affinity-groups page.

**Consequence:** cite the profile PDF as the authority for the club roster, and expect
**no per-club descriptions to exist** for most of them — none are published.

### Year-over-year change

The **2025-26** profile additionally listed **MathCats** and **Book Club**; both are
**absent from the 26-27 edition**. Recorded as a change, not as an error.

The goals > of our affinity groups are to foster kinship, provide students of color a place to > celebrate their uniqueness, gifts and important role in our school community, and…
sections.text:
### Lower School

**Young Children of Color (YCC) — grades K–5**
> "an affinity group and mentoring program for students of color in grades K-5. The goals
> of our affinity groups are to foster kinship, provide students of color a place to
> celebrate their uniqueness, gifts and important role in our school community, and to
> affirm, protect and nurture the racial and cultural identities of the group. **In the
> Lower School all students of color are invited to participate in the program and they
> decide with their parents or guardians whether to participate.**"

**12 Tribes of Trinity — grades 3–5**
> "3rd-5th grade groups of students who learn to build community, internalize and
> reinforce the Honor Code."

(A fuller description appears on the LS Enrichments page — see the traditions file.)

### Middle School

**Young People of Color (YPC)**
> "an affinity group for Middle School students who self identify as students of color at
> Trinity. YPC is designed to provide cultural awareness and affirmation, educational
> preparation for high school, motivation, and social refinement, while enhancing and
> enriching the lives of young students of color in a safe space at TES. **During the year
> the group meets weekly** to discuss a variety of topics, including: cultural sensitivity,
> academic success, and socio-political issues."

**Young People for Social Justice (YPSJ)**
> "an affinity group at Trinity Episcopal School (TES) for **students who self identify as
> white**. Following the words of Gandhi, 'Be the change you wish to see in the world,'
> these groups are intended to provide primarily white students a setting to discuss the
> unearned privilege that is associated with historical and current practices that promote
> injustice and inequality. The groups work to identify the way in which privilege impacts
> the daily lives of students at TES, the community of Charlotte, and the world at large.
> These groups explore ways to impact these societal patterns of injustice as well as
> identify actions that they can take as allies."

**Gender Sexuality Alliance (GSA)**
> "an affinity group that provides an opportunity for middle school students to gather to
> discuss issues and plan activities related to diversity, inclusive of any number of
> topics dealing with human rights. There is a focus on topics inclusive of gay, lesbian,
> bisexual, questioning and transgender issues. The goal of the GSA is to create a safer
> environment for all students and create an open dialogue around the idea of human rights
> and what that looks like for everyone at Trinity and beyond."

sections.text:
Per the data schema, **`affinity` is for IDENTITY groups only.** The five student groups
above qualify. **Chess Club, Odyssey of the Mind, Creative Writing, Monday Math Mania and
the yearbook do NOT** — they belong on the club catalog and academic-clubs cards.

**12 Tribes of Trinity is a genuine edge case**: it appears on the affinity-groups page,
but its own description is about community-building and the Honor Code rather than a
shared identity, and the LS Enrichments page describes it as **co-ed groups spanning
grades 3–5** — a house/advisory system. It is recorded here because the school files it
here, with that caveat noted.

sections.text:
**There is no `/clubs` page.** The 2026-27 School Profile is the only roster, and it is
**a list of names with no descriptions**. Verbatim:

> "**Student Clubs & Groups: Lower School-** Chess Club, Girls on the Run & Let Me Run,
> Young Children of Color, **Middle School-** Odyssey of the Mind, Young People of Color,
> Young People for Social Justice Group, Gender Sexuality Alliance Group, Radagast
> Rabies, Creative Writing, Climate Justice, Koinonia Representatives, Honor Council,
> Invisible Differences, Spirituality and Chapel Music, Monday Math Mania"

**15 named clubs** (3 Lower School, 12 Middle School). Corroboration status, checked against the whole site:

| Club | Division | Corroborated on the site? |
|---|---|---|
| Young Children of Color | LS | ✅ affinity-groups.cfm, with a full purpose statement |
| Young People of Color | MS | ✅ affinity-groups.cfm |
| Young People for Social Justice | MS | ✅ affinity-groups.cfm |
| Gender Sexuality Alliance | MS | ✅ affinity-groups.cfm |
| Honor Council | MS | ✅ spirituality/honor-code.cfm |
| Koinonia Representatives | MS | ✅ Koinonia described on MS Enrichments |
| Chess Club | LS | ⚠️ only as a **paid TED enrichment**, not a club |
| Girls on the Run & Let Me Run | LS | ⚠️ Girls on the Run yes; **Let Me Run: 0 hits** |
| Invisible Differences | listed MS | ⚠️ **is a PARENT group** per affinity-groups.cfm |
| Odyssey of the Mind | MS | ❌ 0 hits |
| Radagast Rabies | MS | ❌ 0 hits |
| Creative Writing | MS | ❌ 0 hits as a club |
| Climate Justice | MS | ❌ 0 hits |
| Monday Math Mania | MS | ❌ 0 hits |
| Spirituality and Chapel Music | MS | ❌ 0 hits |

**Seven of the fifteen have no web corroboration at all**, and **no per-club description
exists for any of them**. Cite the profile PDF and expect nothing further.

**Year-over-year:** the 2025-26 profile also listed **MathCats** and **Book Club**; both
are gone from the 26-27 edition.

### Girls on the Run — the one LS club with real substance

Trinity was the organization's **second independent-school chapter**, it "continues to be
a popular program for students in **grades 3-5**", and founder **Molly Barker** is a
Trinity alumni parent.

### Chess Club is a paid enrichment, not a club

From the TED page, verbatim:
> "TED also offers enrichment programs, **for an additional fee**, several days a week…
> Examples of enrichments include **chess club, music lessons, karate, cheer club** and
> more."

Note "Examples of… and more" — **this is not an exhaustive enrichment list**, and none of
them are priced anywhere.

sections.text:
These are the school's own named rituals, and several are structural rather than
club-like.

### Koinonia — the Middle School advisory system

From MS Enrichments, verbatim:
> "each student belongs to a **Koinonia with 10-12 other Middle School students and one
> adult leader**. Koinonia is a Greek word for 'fellowship' or 'communion' often appearing
> in the New Testament… Koinonia groups gather **every morning for check-in and twice a
> week for activities** that include team-building games; tasks that help develop group
> identity; lessons around diversity, belonging and identity; intramural sports,
> challenges between Koinonias, and discussions specific to the needs of our Middle School
> community."

Its stated purpose:
> "ensures that each student has at least one adult in the school community s/he knows
> well…"

### 12 Tribes of Trinity — the Lower School analogue

From LS Enrichments (fuller than the affinity-groups version), verbatim:
> "Based on the Biblical 12 Tribes of Israel, Trinity Tribes are **co-ed groups of
> students in grades 3-5** that provide the opportunity for students from different grade
> levels to get to know one another, engage in meaningful activities together, and build
> relationships. **Each Tribe is led by 2 adult staculty members.**"

### Science Buddies — 8th grade ↔ Kindergarten

From `/academics/middle-school.cfm`, verbatim:
> "Our **8th Graders cherish the time they spend with our kindergartners as Science
> Buddies** and look forward to their class trip to Washington, D. C., where they meet with
> lobbyists and legislators to advocate for a social issue they've studied and researched
> all year in their Social Issues Seminar class."

### RISE — 5th grade transition programme

From LS Enrichments, verbatim:
> "In the last trimester of **5th Grade**, students split into **gender-based small groups
> for the RISE program** to develop personal leadership skills that build confidence for
> the transition to Middle School."

### Greet the Week — Monday mornings

From `/spirituality/chapel.cfm`, verbatim:
> "All staculty and students gather in **Jamie's Courtyard** each Monday morning to start
> the week with scripture, prayer, songs, the Pledge of Allegiance, our Honor Code and
> general student-led school announcements for that week."

The profile PDF's shorter version:
> "Monday mornings, the school gathers as a community to begin the week with songs, Bible
> verses, the Lord's Prayer and announcements."

**Chapel rhythm:** bi-weekly K–2 and 3–5 chapels, weekly 6–8 chapel, and a **K–8 chapel
every Friday in the Gym**.

sections.subtopic: A grade-by-grade service ladder with 12 named partners
sections.preview: This is a curricular programme, not a volunteer club — every grade has a standing partnership tied to its curriculum. The school's framing, verbatim: > "Regular and meaningful service activity in our local and global community is intended > to open children's eyes to the broader world, develop service as a habit of…
sections.text:
This is a **curricular** programme, not a volunteer club — every grade has a standing
partnership tied to its curriculum.

The school's framing, verbatim:
> "Regular and meaningful service activity in our local and global community is intended
> to open children's eyes to the broader world, develop service as a habit of the heart
> and intentionally challenge students to step out of their comfort zones."

> "Each grade level partners with a community organization whose mission and services are
> related to curricular goals… **Year-long partnerships create the possibility of
> relationship formation that transforms charity into mutual service among neighbors.**"

| Grade | Partner(s) | Theme / detail |
|---|---|---|
| **K** | Nourish Up | Hunger and social isolation; students deliver **Meals on Wheels** weekly |
| **1** | Nourish Up | Visit the **Nourish Up Food Pantry at First Presbyterian Church**; lead a school **Food Drive in November**; deliver groceries with parents |
| **2** | InReach | Adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities; a self-advocacy class at the **Baxter St. community center** and **Covenant Presbyterian Church**; InReach customers visit Trinity **monthly** for gardening, art, music and self-advocacy |
| **3** | **Roof Above** / Urban Ministry Center | Homelessness; students **walk a mile to the Urban Ministry Center** monthly for art, soccer, **singing with the Urban Ministry Choir**, and clothing drives |
| **4** | The Epiphany School of Charlotte | Children with physical, cognitive and social differences; reciprocal relationships |
| **5** | Galilee Ministries of East Charlotte | "Housed in the former St. Andrew's Episcopal Church on Central Avenue… a special mission of the Episcopal Diocese of North Carolina… services to refugees, immigrants, migrants, and neighbors in East Charlotte." |
| **6** | 8th Street Friendship Garden · Charlotte Community ToolBank · NourishUp | **"Feeding Our Neighbors"** — crop rotations, growth cycles, food scarcity |
| **7** | Crisis Assistance Ministry · Hope Haven · First Ward Child Development Center | **"Understanding Our Neighbors"** — houselessness, addiction, poverty, human trafficking |
| **8** | *(no named partner)* | **"Advocacy and Social Action"** — community mapping, a Social Issues Seminar research project, and a **capstone advocacy trip to Washington, DC** |

**12 named partner organizations** across grades K–7.

> ⚠️ **Two naming inconsistencies in the school's own copy — preserve them:**
> - Grade 3 is **headed** "Roof Above" but the **body** says "Urban Ministry of
> Charlotte" / "Urban Ministry Center". Roof Above is the renamed organization; both
> names appear on the page.
> - Grade 6 spells it **"NourishUp"** (no space) while K and 1 spell it **"Nourish Up"**.
> Both spellings are the school's own.

From the Head of School's welcome page, verbatim:

> "We like to say that **Trinity has the longest hallways in Charlotte** as our campus
> community extends into the heart of Uptown Charlotte. Each day you will see our students
> and teachers walking to and engaging with community organizations as part of our
> academic program and service-learning partnerships."

> ⚠️ This quote is on **`/about/`**, NOT the service-learning page. Cite it correctly.

This is the mechanism behind the grade-3 partnership — students **walk** to the Urban
Ministry Center. A 4.5-acre uptown campus is what makes a walking service programme
possible, and the school says so explicitly.

sections.text:
From the May 2024 account (threadid=15): **46 eighth-graders** travelled to Washington.

Assistant Head of School **Stephanie Griffin**, verbatim:
> "This is a trip, at its heart and soul, that's all about advocacy."

Topics students advocated on: **gun-violence victim resources, economic mobility, minimum
wage, affordable housing, and healthcare cost transparency**.

They met **Rep. Jeff Jackson** at the U.S. Capitol, plus staff for Reps. Alma Adams, Dan
Bishop, Deborah Ross and Bobby Scott, and Sens. Budd, Tillis, Capito, Hickenlooper, Brown
and Murphy. They also met **Moms Demand Action**, the **U.S. Department of Labor**, and
the **National Low Income Housing Coalition**.

The trip is tied to the **Social Issues Seminar (8)**, a weekly enrichment — so the
capstone is curricular, not extracurricular.

Related civic programming in the blog: an 8th-grade advocacy panel, a transit-vote
exercise giving 8th grade "a glimpse at the election process", and students witnessing a
**Walk for Peace** during a Charlotte visit.
